preamble: Th-fronting of the voiced dental fricative [ð] to labiodental [v], mostly word-medially and finally, since [ð] usually does not front word-initially (that is rarely 'vat'). It is common in Cockney, Essex and Estuary English, Manchester English and African American Vernacular English.

examples.note: Also further > furver, either, father; function words like the, they are not affected.
Th-fronting is listed for AAVE, chiefly in non-initial position.
